1. When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 10–25% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.  
2. If sentiment spikes to 1.00+ and prices are trending upward, model often overreacts — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 20% below true outcome.  
3. For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model frequently overshoots — apply 20–40% downward adjustment to forecast tail.  
4. When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.67) and history shows mean-reverting pattern, model tends to lag — add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 1–7d horizon to catch momentum.  
5. If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33 and true outcome is consistently low, model overestimates — apply 30–50% downward bias for 10–30d horizon.  
6. For 30d forecasts, if model shows high volatility (e.g., >3x range) with no sentiment signal, reduce forecast variance — use 20% smoothing or median-based adjustment.
